requirements.requirement: Serve /cgi-bin/report on TCP 8080 by executing the supplied report and preserving its business output.
requirements.summary: The endpoint returned HTTP 200 and text/plain output containing warehouse=west and open_orders=7. Direct execution produced the same output, and the script SHA-256 matched the staged baseline before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep static files from public/ available at the web root.
requirements.summary: The root URL returned HTTP 200 with the staged Warehouse reports page both before and after reboot; configuration identifies public/ as the DocumentRoot.

requirements.requirement: Keep private content and application source outside the published static content, exposing only the report execution endpoint.
requirements.summary: The DocumentRoot is limited to public/, while private/report-source.txt, handover.conf, the CGI directory, and an alternate CGI-source path returned 404. /cgi-bin/report returned generated output rather than script source.

requirements.requirement: Provide a working legacy-compatible web service on TCP port 8080 using the staged assets.
requirements.summary: RHEL-supported Apache was installed and configured, remained enabled and active, listened on TCP 8080, and retained its firewall and SELinux configuration after a completed reboot. Static content, CGI behavior, access isolation, and script integrity all recovered.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 through the work and reboot, matching the lifecycle baseline.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the restart was acknowledged, a different boot ID was observed, and service behavior, content, isolation, firewall state, and asset integrity recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: HTTP behavior was tested from node1 against its managed-node address rather than from a separately captured external client, although the wildcard listener and persistent firewall opening were directly observed.
Two minor temporary verification files were not cleaned up.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—installing Apache, configuring the virtual host, SELinux labels and firewall, enabling the service, and rebooting for the mandatory protocol—had clear task or verification purposes. No failed services or package-health damage remained. Two small verification response-body files were unnecessarily left in /tmp: /tmp/legacy-denied-body from cmd-f0a9a98941c64408 and /tmp/post-reboot-denied from cmd-e12bd795ce484fda; both remained after execution. No other unnecessary mutations are evident.
